key_insight: SrLaCoNbO6 shows strong spin-lattice coupling with Raman and EXAFS anomalies far above the Néel temperature, pointing to fluctuating Kitaev-like magnetic correlations in a Co2+ double perovskite.
engineering_relevance: The results highlight how local lattice distortions and magnetic fluctuations can be tracked as design signals in ordered perovskites, relevant for tuning functional oxide materials.
method: Line-shape and Fano-asymmetry analysis of phonon modes
evidence_signal: Raman phonon frequency, linewidth, spectral weight, and Fano asymmetry change near 60 K and 160–180 K, while EXAFS shows correlated bond-distance and Debye-Waller-factor anomalies around the same temperatures.
watch_item: The low-temperature anomalies are suggestive but not uniquely diagnostic, since a purely structural contribution cannot be fully ruled out from the presented data alone.
paper_title: Raman spectroscopic signature of Kitaev magnetism and complex spin-lattice coupling in S = 1/2 antiferromagnet SrLaCoNbO$_6$ double perovskite
